question: The roots of \(x^3+2x^2-x+3\) are \(p\), \(q\), and \(r\). What is the value of \[ (p^2+4)(q^2+4)(r^2+4)? \]
solution:
The requested product is symmetric in the roots, so Vieta's formulas let us evaluate it without finding the roots. They give
\[
p+q+r=-2,\qquad pq+pr+qr=-1,\qquad pqr=-3.
\]
Squaring the first relation gives
\[
p^2+q^2+r^2
=(p+q+r)^2-2(pq+pr+qr)
=4+2=6.
\]
For the squared pairwise products, expanding a square gives
\[
(pq+pr+qr)^2
=p^2q^2+p^2r^2+q^2r^2+2pqr(p+q+r).
\]
Therefore
\[
p^2q^2+p^2r^2+q^2r^2
=(-1)^2-2(-3)(-2)=-11.
\]
Also, \(p^2q^2r^2=(pqr)^2=9\). Expanding the requested product now yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
(p^2+4)(q^2+4)(r^2+4)
&=p^2q^2r^2+4(p^2q^2+p^2r^2+q^2r^2)\\
&\quad+16(p^2+q^2+r^2)+64\\
&=9+4(-11)+16(6)+64\\
&=\boxed{125}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
